note: Which devpod flags consume the next argv element, for both fake devpods.
A fake devpod has to know this to find a subcommand's positional at all: read
`--init-env` as a bare flag and `DL_WORKSPACE_ID=owner-repo-main` becomes the
workspace source. Real devpod is a cobra program, so it takes a value flag on
either side of the positional, and only the leading position tells the two
apart -- which is why growing these lists one flag at a time is how they went
wrong: `--init-env`, `--mount`, `--dotfiles-script`, `--dotfiles-script-env`
and `--workspace-env-file` were all missing from a table that production
sends them to.
The lists lived twice, once per fake, with nothing comparing them. They live
here now, for the same reason `conformance.json` beside this file does: two
hand-written copies of one fact drift, and the drift is invisible to any test
of either copy against itself. Each fake reads this file; neither keeps its
own, and a test on each side says so.
Every list is taken from `devpod <verb> --help` at v0.26.1 wholesale rather
than grown as flags were needed: every flag it types `string`, `strings`,
`stringArray` or a named type is here, and the booleans (`--recreate`,
`--reset`, `--open-ide`, `--force`, `--ignore-not-found`,
`--container-status`) are not, because cobra takes a boolean's value only as
`--flag=false`.
`global` is the flag block every subcommand inherits; `--debug` and
`--silent` are bare and so are absent. `stop` has no flags of its own at
v0.26.1, and its empty list is a fact rather than an oversight -- both fakes
assert it stays empty on both sides.
The keys are the roll call: both drivers name the same six and fail on a
table that appears here without them, or on one either fake defines for
itself instead of reading it here.
